parts:
Hello,

I've been trying to do a multiple group analysis using gender, but I get this error.

Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan ERROR: some categories of variable `Q5005C' are empty in group 1; frequencies are [268 11 8 0]

This is the code I've been using:
Mod5='Fy~f1+f2+f3+f4
f1=~Q7505+Q7510+Q7515
f2=~Q400+Q405+Q410+Q415
f3=~Q5005A+Q5005B+Q5005C+Q5005D+Q5005E+Q5005F+Q5005G+Q5005H
f4=~Q505A+Q505B+Q505C+Q505D+Q505E+Q505F+Q505G+Q505H+Q505I+Q505J+Q505K+Q505M
Fy=~Q1755A+Q1755B+Q1755C+Q1755D+Q1755E+Q1755F'

fit5=sem(Mod5, data=W2c, group="Q210")

Does anyone know how I can fix this?

Thanks!

Beth,
I jumped the gun with my previous post. However, I was just able to
reproduce your error message by adding my reproduction of your variable
to the first 287 cases of the HolzingerSwineford1939 data that comes
with lavaan. Your frequencies are very low for all but one value of
the variable. If you crosstabulate the variable with your grouping
variable, you may find that the variable is constant in one of your
groups (below "school" is the grouping variable and
"FactorExampleFixed" mimics your variable).

> table(HolzingerSwineford1939$school[1:287], FactorExampleFixed)
FactorExampleFixed
First Second Third
Grant-White 112 11 8
Pasteur 156 0 0

That's not a software problem. Hayduk (1996) suggested an approach
that would allow you to include the variable in the data for one group
but not the data for the other group. However, you may want to simply
drop the variable from your model.

Hayduk, L. A. (1996). LISREL: Issues, dabates & strategies.
Baltimore, MD: Johns Hopkins.

Keith
